content: 1. Progestin is prescribed for females of reproductive potential to prevent pregnancy. The regimen involves taking one tablet daily for 28 consecutive days, with one white active tablet per day for the first 24 days, followed by one green inert tablet per day for the remaining 4 days. 2. This medication is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 3. Before initiating this product, consider the possibility of ovulation and conception. 4. Progestin is not indicated for premenarcheal females. 5. The safety and efficacy of this medication have been established in females of reproductive age. It is expected to have similar safety and efficacy in postpubertal adolescents under 16 years of age and those aged 16 years or older. Refer to adult dosing guidelines. 6. Amiloride and drospirenone both increase serum potassium levels. Their combined use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia, as they enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. 7. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of drospirenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Belzutifan may cause contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding when used with hormonal contraceptives. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan can cause fetal harm. 8. Calaspargase pegol and drospirenone interaction is of unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Due to the potential for indirect interaction between calaspargase pegol and oral contraceptives, concomitant use is not recommended. Use a non-oral contraceptive method for females of childbearing potential. 9. Drospirenone and eplerenone both increase serum potassium levels through pharmacodynamic synergism. Their combined use is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 10. Drospirenone increases the level or effect of fedratinib. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining fedratinib, a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate, with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors, as the effect of such coadministration has not been studied. 11. Mavacamten may reduce systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during coadministration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 13.
